Crm (A)/3841/2024 on 12 November, 2024
 12.11.2024
 14
 as
 [Allowed]
 C. R. M. (A) 3841 of 2024
 In Re: An application for anticipatory bail under Section 48
 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in connection
 with Bowbazar Police Station Case No. 115 of 2023 dated
 17.06.2023 under Sections 406/420/120B of the Indian Penal
 Code.

In Re: Amit Kumar Roy & Anr.
 ... ... Petitioner  Mr. Debabrata Acharyya,
Mr. Sital Samanta.

for the petitioners  Mr. Antarikhya Basu,
 Mr. Aslam Parvez.
 ... ... for the Stat  1.
Petitioners submit they are co-owners of the land and a development agreement was executed between them and the de- facto complainant/developer.
The developer did not act in terms of the agreement.
Petitioners revoked the development agreement/power of attorney and entered into a new agreement with a third party.
In retaliation, a criminal case has been registered.

Accordingly,
they pray for anticipatory bail.
2. Learned Advocate for the State submits petitioners had taken a sum of Rs.28 lakhs from the de-facto complainant.
Subsequently, they have entered into a new agreement with a third party.
3. We have considered the materials on record.
A development agreement was executed by and between the petitioners and the de-facto complainant.

Subsequently, the agreement and power of attorney were revoked and a fresh Signed By : ALOK SETH High Court of Calcutta 13 th of November 2024 05:54:41 PM agreement has been executed between the petitioners and a third party.
Non-refund of the advance made under the revoked agreement is a civil dispute which cannot partake a criminal profile.
4. Under such circumstances, we are of the opinion petitioners may be granted anticipatory bail.

CRM (A)/3841/2024 on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196435580/
1 5.

Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest, the petitioners viz., Amit Kumar Roy and Moumita Roy be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- each, with two sureties of like amount each, to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer and also subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.
They shall appear before the jurisdictional court and pray for regular bail within four weeks from date.
6. The application for anticipatory bail is, thus, disposed of.

(Gaurang Kanth, J.) (Joymalya Bagchi,
J.)
Signed By : ALOK SETH High Court of Calcutta 13 th of November 2024 05:54:41 PM CRM (A)/3841/2024 on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196435580/
